To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the allotypic determinant(s) on antigen-specific suppressor (Ts) and enhancing (Ta) T cells are encoded by genes on the Igh-1 gene cluster, and that the genes are distinct from those encoding the allotypic B cell Igh determinants.

the antigen-specific augmenter (TaF) or suppressor (Ts) factors of the antigen-specific T cell population, which are responsible for the antigen-induced enhancement or suppression of antibody production, respectively, express two distinct allotypic (probably constant region) determinants on their antigen-recognition units, which are distinct from the B cell Igb allotypes.

the antigen-specific T cell factors are composed of two different allotypic subunits (allodeterminants distinct from the B cell Igs allotypes), and that the genes coding for them are located in the B cell Igb-V gene cluster on the 12 chromosome of the mouse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new allotypic system of the T cell antigen receptor, which is distinct from that of the B cell antigen receptor, and is encoded by the genes linked to the B cell IGH locus.

the genetic and functional analysis of the antigen-specific T cell factors, and has revealed that the T cell factors are encoded by genes distinct from the immunoglobulin V region genes and are accommodated somewhere in or near the right side of Igh-V.
a new type of T cell allotype, which is encoded by genes linked with the B cell IGH-V gene cluster, and is distinct from the B cell Iga and Igh allotypes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are two allotypic determinations on the antigen-specific TsF and TaF molecules, which are distinct from those on B cell Igh.
the two distinct T cell allodetemnins are encoded by two genes, one of which is located in the right end of the Igh-V gene cluster on chromosome 12 and the other is located in the Igh-C region.

the Igh-V gene cluster is the site where genes for the antigen-recognition unit of T cell factors, and the genes for the B cell constant region, and for the antigen-recognitive unit of the T cell receptor, are located.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the antigen-binding units of T cell factors are encoded by genes located in the B cell IGH-V gene cluster, and that the antigen-specific T cell factors have two antigen-recognition units, which may have different functions in the regulation of immune responses.
the T cell allotype is encoded by genes located in the right end of the 12th mouse chromosome, and that the genes are expressed only on a subset of T cells.

the antigen-specific T cells, as well as the antigen-specific suppressive and enhancing T cell factor, are encoded by genes that are linked to the immunoglobin heavy chain locus, and that the T cell factors are encoded by the genes in the same order as that in the B cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antigen-recognition unit of the antigen-specific TsF is different from that of the TaF.
the Igh-1 locus is not only responsible for the production of B cells but also for the production of T cell factors.

the T cell allotypes are not only encoded by the Igh locus, but also are distinct from those on B cells, and that the genes coding for the determinant(s) of the antigen-specific T cell factors are linked to the Igh-V gene cluster.
